correctness.rationale: Mass and Hamiltonian energy are conserved for all time. The time-rescaled finite-dimensional polynomial flow is analytic in inverse Kerr coupling on every compact scaled-time interval. The coefficient at each site vanishes below graph distance and obeys a shortest-path recursion at the first nonzero order. Neighbor second-order terms sum to (A^3)oo=2 rooted triangles and give the exact signed next-order leakage. Energy conservation, a half-mass barrier, and a uniform quadratic leakage inequality give all-time limsup 4d; evaluating the local expansion at s=pi gives liminf 4d. The embedded verifier independently passed 117 finite sanity checks, not used as proof.
